title: Chat rooms
statement: The gateway MUST provide multi-user chat rooms with streamed assistant replies.

title: Reply metadata
statement: Every reply MUST carry reasoning_mode (fast or slow), assurance level, tokens used, thinking budget used and wall-clock cost.

title: Conversation context
statement: The Context Manager MUST assemble prompts from conversation history within the configured context cap and SHOULD preserve prompt-cache prefixes.

title: Speed-care control
statement: Users MAY set a single scalar lambda (speed-care) per conversation; the gate MUST use it as the cost price.

title: Model profiles
statement: Operators MUST be able to select model profile A, B or C by configuration without code changes.

title: Controller events
statement: The gateway MUST stream controller events (gate decision, verification result, retry, abstention) alongside tokens.

title: Gate features
statement: The Aql Gate MUST compute, from the fast draft, the features: mean and minimum token log-probability, agreement among k samples, domain class and, for verifiable tasks, the verifier outcome.

title: Derived gate rule
statement: The gate MUST escalate iff L*(e1_hat - e2_hat) > lambda*delta_c using a calibrated estimator e1_hat and per-domain e2_hat; hand-tuned score thresholds MUST NOT be used in production mode.

title: Failed verification escalates
statement: A verifiable task whose fast draft fails verification MUST be escalated and MUST NOT be returned as kept.

title: Decision record
statement: For every request the gate MUST write a decision record containing features, estimates, threshold, lambda, configuration hash and outcome.

title: Budget mode
statement: Operators MAY configure an escalation budget B instead of lambda; the gate MUST then use the multiplier lambda* from the empirical quantile with the DKW sample-size rule.

title: Gate recalibration
statement: The calibration estimator MUST be retrained from the ledger on a configured schedule and MUST NOT be promoted unless NFR-020 holds on held-out data.

title: Sequential verified sampling
statement: System 2 MUST draw candidates sequentially, verify each, stop at the first accepted candidate, and respect caps N per round and R rounds.

title: Caps from Phase-0 fit
statement: N and R per domain MUST be derived from the Phase-0 Beta fit of acceptance rates and the configured cost ratio c_p/L_a, and the derivation MUST be recorded with the configuration.

title: No unverified refinement
statement: On non-verifiable tasks R MUST be at most 1 and no refinement MAY replace an earlier candidate without a verifier or judge acceptance.

title: Draft-blind deliberation
statement: System 2 MUST NOT receive the fast draft by default; draft-conditioned mode MAY exist only as an ablation flag that is off in production.

title: Thinking budget and forcing
statement: Each domain MUST have a thinking budget; on exhaustion the controller MUST force the answer by closing the reasoning span and, if no answer results, return an abstention with notice.

title: Evidence-fed retry
statement: A rejected candidate's verifier evidence MUST be included in the next round's prompt.

title: Bounded loop
statement: The orchestrator MUST enforce the model-call cap 1+N(R+1) and a wall-clock cap per request, terminating in state T or X.

title: Exact verifiers
statement: The Verifier Hub MUST provide exact verifiers for code (test execution in a sandbox), mathematics (numeric and symbolic equality against a reference) and JSON Schema validity.

title: Assurance levels
statement: Every reply MUST carry one of the assurance levels verified, consensus, unverified or abstained, and consensus MUST NOT be presented as verified.

title: Verifier rates
statement: Each verifier MUST publish (r, phi) measured by mutation testing; exact verifiers MUST use acceptance threshold 1.0.

title: Consensus not training data
statement: Consensus-assured outputs MUST NOT enter the distillation set without human review.

title: Judge hard gate
statement: The rubric judge MUST apply hard floors honesty >= 0.5, harm-avoidance >= 0.5, helpfulness >= 0.5 and total V >= 0.7 before any candidate is accepted on non-verifiable tasks.

title: Code sandbox
statement: Code verification MUST run in a subprocess with CPU-time, memory, wall-clock and output limits, no network and an ephemeral file system.

title: Audit stream
statement: A random fraction epsilon (default 0.05) of kept requests MUST also be run through System 2 offline and recorded as audits.

title: Capability table
statement: The Muhasaba Ledger MUST produce per-domain capability statistics keyed by model and adapter hash and MUST report domains without audited data as unmeasured.

title: Drift monitoring
statement: The ledger MUST run a CUSUM chart on calibration error and accuracy per domain with a negative control and raise an alert on change.

title: Evaluation harness
statement: The Eval Harness MUST run benchmark sets through the gateway API for the system and for the fast-only and slow-only baselines and compute the metrics of ER-010.

title: Paired statistics
statement: The harness MUST report paired differences with confidence intervals, non-inferiority tests and Bonferroni correction across domains.

title: Performance console
statement: The performance console MUST run load tests against the gateway and report latency quantiles, throughput, escalation rate and cost per request.

title: Gate dashboard
statement: The dashboard MUST display the go/no-go status of each roadmap gate from stored evaluation runs.

title: Persistent store
statement: Conversations, decision records and traces MUST be stored (SQLite and JSONL) with a configurable retention period.

title: Retrieval memory
statement: The Context Manager MAY retrieve prior verified answers with an embedding index; retrieved text MUST be delimited as data with provenance.

title: Distillation dataset builder
statement: The dataset builder MUST select verified System 2 traces, deduplicate, cap any domain at 30 percent, and add 5 percent abstention examples.

title: Hard latency bound
statement: Every request MUST terminate within the configured wall-clock cap (default 300 s on the CPU baseline), returning an abstention if necessary. Target.

title: Fast-path first token
statement: Target: on the reference machine, time to first token of the fast path SHOULD be <= 2 s at p95 for prompts <= 1000 tokens with prompt cache hits.

title: Fast-path reply latency
statement: Target: a 150-token fast-path reply SHOULD complete within 12 s at p95 on the reference machine (Profile A).

title: Slow-path latency
statement: Target: a slow-path reply with a 1024-token thinking budget on the 4B model SHOULD complete within 240 s at p95 on the reference machine.

title: Memory budget
statement: Resident memory of both model servers, KV cache and the gateway MUST stay below 8 GB in Profile A on the CPU baseline.

title: Context cap
statement: The CPU baseline MUST cap prompts at 4096 tokens and MUST enable prompt caching on the model servers.

title: Concurrency
statement: Target: the reference CPU machine SHOULD serve its recommended concurrency limit of 2 chat sessions with p95 fast-path latency at most twice the single-session value; 4 concurrent sessions are a GPU-profile target (restated by the owner on 2026-10-21, decision 002: on four cores the four-session p95 is 3.4 to 3.9x and no slot count reaches 2x).

title: Backend resilience
statement: The gateway MUST survive model-server restarts, reconnect automatically and lose no decision records or traces.

title: Backpressure
statement: In-flight requests per backend MUST be bounded by configuration and excess requests MUST receive HTTP 429 with a retry hint.

title: Pinned model identity
statement: Model identifiers, revisions, quantisation, chat-template hash and configuration hash MUST be recorded in every trace.

title: Gate calibration
statement: Target: the calibration error (ECE with 5 bins on >= 2900 held-out samples) of e1_hat MUST be <= 0.05 before a calibration is promoted.

title: Observability
statement: The gateway MUST expose Prometheus metrics, structured JSON logs and OpenTelemetry spans carrying the request identifier.

title: Access control
statement: API access MUST require a bearer token; rate limits MUST apply per token; secrets MUST NOT appear in logs or traces.

title: Build reproducibility
statement: Cargo.lock MUST be committed, CI MUST build and test on Linux and macOS, and evaluation runs MUST use recorded random seeds.

title: OpenAPI document
statement: The gateway MUST publish an OpenAPI 3.1 document equal to spec/openapi.yaml at /openapi.json.

title: Chat endpoints
statement: The gateway MUST provide POST /v1/chat for complete replies and POST /v1/chat/stream for SSE with event types token, decision, verification, retry, done and error.

title: Reasoning mode in replies
statement: The reply schema MUST include reasoning_mode, assurance, usage and decision_id fields.

title: Chat-room WebSocket
statement: Chat rooms MUST be served over WebSocket at /ws/rooms/{room_id} with JSON frames defined in the schemas.

title: JSON Schemas
statement: ChatRequest, ChatReply, DecisionRecord, TraceRecord and VerifierResult MUST be defined as JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) files and generated from the Rust types.

title: Backend contract
statement: Model backends MUST be reached through the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions API with logprobs, n and chat_template_kwargs, and reasoning content MUST be separated by the server parser.

title: Retry policy
statement: Backend calls MUST be retried at most 3 times with exponential backoff and jitter on connection errors and HTTP 5xx, never on HTTP 4xx, and only when the request is idempotent.

title: Backend backpressure
statement: Each backend MUST have a concurrency semaphore sized to the server's maximum sequences, and queued requests MUST time out with a distinct error.

title: Bench and eval endpoints
statement: The gateway MUST provide /v1/bench/runs and /v1/eval/runs resources to start, list and fetch runs.

title: Telemetry format
statement: Traces MUST be newline-delimited JSON records conforming to TraceRecord with a schema_version field.

title: Pinned models
statement: Profile A MUST pin Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B (System 1) and Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 (System 2) by repository revision and GGUF file hash.

title: Thinking toggle
statement: The backend layer MUST set thinking on or off per request through chat_template_kwargs or model selection, and MUST reject replies whose reasoning content is not separated.

title: Serving configurations
statement: The specification MUST provide a vLLM-CPU launch configuration for Linux and a llama-server command for macOS or AVX2 hosts exposing the same API.

title: Degraded mode
statement: If the System 2 backend is unavailable the gateway MUST answer with the fast path, label the reply unverified, and emit a degraded-mode event.

title: Profile C adoption
statement: Profile C (Qwen3.5) MUST NOT become the default unless hypothesis H7 (decode speed >= 70 percent of dense Qwen3 at equal size on the target CPU) passes at gate G0 or G5.

title: SFT data schema
statement: Training examples MUST follow the JSONL schema with fields id, domain, prompt, answer, rationale (<= 150 tokens), assurance, verifier, source_trace, adapter_hash.

title: Verified-only training data
statement: Only traces with assurance verified, plus human-reviewed consensus traces, MAY enter the training set.

title: Synthetic data
statement: Synthetic examples MUST be generated by System 2 on benchmark-like prompts, verified by an exact verifier never used for evaluation, and labelled synthetic.

title: Unsloth configuration
statement: Fine-tuning MUST use Unsloth LoRA with rank 16, alpha 16, learning rate 2e-4, 1 to 3 epochs, effective batch 16, dropout 0 on all attention and MLP projections; QLoRA for Qwen3 checkpoints and BF16 LoRA for Qwen3.5 checkpoints.

title: GPU path
statement: Training MUST run on a GPU host (minimum 16 GB VRAM); the CPU machine MUST NOT be used for training.

title: Checkpoints and export
statement: Each training run MUST produce an adapter with a content hash, a merged GGUF in q4_k_m and q8_0, and a manifest linking data snapshot, configuration and hashes.

title: Promotion gate
statement: An adapter MAY be promoted only if the lower confidence bound of the overall gain on a held-out verifier is above zero with point estimate >= 2 points, no domain's lower bound is below -1 point, NFR-020 and the coupling test still pass, and a human signs off.

title: Replay and abstention
statement: Training sets MUST include 20 percent replay of general instruction data and 5 percent abstention examples.

title: Prompt-injection handling
statement: Retrieved content, tool output and verifier evidence MUST be delimited as data in prompts; nothing in model output or observed content MAY change controller parameters or configuration.

title: Sandbox isolation
statement: The code sandbox MUST run without network access, under resource limits and, on Linux, under seccomp or a container; sandbox escapes MUST be tested.

title: Content safety
statement: Replies on non-verifiable tasks MUST pass the judge's harm floor; refused requests MUST return a refusal with an explanation and no partial content.

title: Privacy
statement: Users MUST be informed that conversations may be used for evaluation and training; retention MUST be bounded; personal data MUST be redacted before training; opt-out MUST exclude a conversation.

title: Religious content
statement: User-facing copy MUST describe the nafs and aql terms as analogies, MUST NOT claim religious authority, and the analogy text MUST be reviewed by a scholar of the tradition before release.

title: Transport and secrets
statement: Deployments MUST terminate TLS in front of the gateway and load secrets from the environment or a secret store.

title: Build and CI
statement: The Cargo workspace MUST build with the pinned toolchain; CI MUST run fmt, clippy, unit and integration tests on every push.

title: Packaging
statement: Releases MUST ship a gateway binary, a model manifest with SHA-256 hashes and the configuration schema.

title: Deployment recipes
statement: The specification MUST include docker-compose for the Linux vLLM-CPU profile and service files for the llama-server profile.

title: Monitoring and alerts
statement: Dashboards and alerts MUST cover latency, error rate, escalation rate, verifier acceptance and calibration drift.

title: Rollback
statement: Adapter or model promotion MUST be a configuration change; the previous artefact MUST be retained and restorable with one command.

title: Configuration management
statement: All runtime parameters MUST live in one TOML file validated against a schema, with environment overrides, and the configuration hash MUST appear in traces.

title: Phase-0 baseline size
statement: The Phase-0 measurement run MUST include at least 4600 tasks across at least five domains.

title: Non-inferiority gates
statement: The cascade MUST be non-inferior to the slow-only baseline within 3 points on >= 700 pairs at gate G2 and within 1 point on >= 6200 pairs at gate G6.

title: Verifier mutation tests
statement: Each verifier MUST be evaluated on >= 200 mutants with Clopper-Pearson intervals on (r, phi).

title: Coupling test
statement: The draft-blind and draft-conditioned modes MUST each be tested on >= 200 trials for adoption of a wrong draft.

title: Calibration test
statement: Calibration MUST be evaluated with 5 bins on >= 2900 held-out samples.

title: Unit coverage
statement: Line coverage of nafs-core MUST be >= 80 percent and every automaton transition MUST have a test.

title: Load test protocol
statement: Load tests MUST use the recorded protocol (goose, fixed prompt set, 1, 2, 4 concurrent sessions) and report p50, p95, p99.

title: Regression suite
statement: A fixed regression suite MUST run on every model, adapter, template or configuration change before promotion.

title: Metric definitions
statement: The harness MUST implement the metrics of the specification Section 10 with the stated formulas and unit tests on synthetic data.

title: Hybrid-model benchmark
statement: Phase 0 MUST benchmark Qwen3.5-2B and 4B against Qwen3-1.7B and 4B with llama-bench on the target CPU.

title: Latency attribution
statement: Every reply MUST record per-stage timings (retrieval, draft, samples, verification, deliberation, judge) and, for model stages, the queue wait, prefill and decode time and KV-cache reuse reported by the server; the gateway MUST report each stage's share of wall time.

title: Interleaved tuning evidence
statement: A serving-flag or weight-format change MUST be justified by an interleaved A/B (alternating order, at least two rounds) on the reference machine, with the host load recorded.

title: Early escalation
statement: Under the fixed rule the gate SHOULD stop an unverifiable draft once its running mean log-prob after a minimum number of tokens is below the threshold minus a margin, and escalate; its decisions MUST agree with full-draft decisions on at least 95% of a held-out prompt set before it is on by default.

title: Speculative decoding heads
statement: Each model MAY be served with a trained speculative head (EAGLE-3) or an n-gram drafter, enabled only where a measured decode speed-up of at least 1.2x holds with identical greedy output.

title: Efficiency frontier
statement: The lab MUST report, per domain, the accuracy-latency frontier of System 1 / System 2 policies including early escalation, with saved draft tokens and routing agreement.

title: Adaptive reasoning exit
statement: System 2 reasoning SHOULD be probed at reflection points (and at least every configured interval) for a short answer; on verifiable tasks the exact verifier MAY end the reasoning early, and on other tasks agreement between consecutive probes MAY; the final answer MUST be generated after the reasoning as on the standard path, and the exit reason MUST be recorded.

title: Lowest-window confidence
statement: The gate MUST record the lowest mean log-prob over any configured window of consecutive draft tokens as a feature; under the fixed rule, for the configured domains, a draft whose lowest window is below the configured threshold MUST be escalated and MAY be stopped the moment the crossing is observed, since the signal is a running minimum (the early decision equals the full-draft decision).

title: Posterior exit rule
statement: On non-verifiable tasks the adaptive reasoning exit SHOULD support stopping when the posterior probability that the plurality probe answer is the majority answer (Dirichlet(1) prior over all probes) reaches a bound that is non-increasing in the reasoning budget used; the rule in force and the posterior MUST be recorded on every probe.

title: Agreement samples on unverified drafts
statement: For configured domains, a draft that no exact verifier can check MUST receive the k agreement samples after the draft regardless of its token confidence, and the agreement feature MUST be recorded; the domain list MUST be justified by a stored study showing agreement predicts a wrong draft better than token confidence.

title: Confidence-signal study
statement: The gate's confidence signal MUST be chosen by a stored study that reports, per candidate signal, the ROC and AUROC (with a bootstrap interval) for predicting a wrong draft against exact labels, and the recall of wrong drafts at the operating escalation rate; a signal is adopted only if its ROC dominates at that rate.

title: Room lifecycle
statement: A room MUST be creatable, renamable and deletable over the API. Names MUST be normalised (control characters dropped, whitespace collapsed, at most 80 characters) and unique without regard to case (409 on a clash); a gateway MUST bound the number of rooms. Deleting a room MUST remove, in one transaction, the room, its conversation and messages and the replies, decisions, audits, feedback, reviews, preference trials and retrieval-memory entries made from it, MUST notify and disconnect its members, and MUST cancel a running answer so that nothing of the room remains once it has stopped.

title: Room join snapshot
statement: The first frame a member of a room receives MUST be a welcome frame with the name assigned to it (unique in the room), the members, the assistant's state, the limits, a history cursor and the pending questions, taken together with the subscription so that every turn reaches the member exactly once, whether it joined early, late or while an answer was being written.

title: Room resilience
statement: A room MUST bound its members, the length of a message (refused, never truncated), the queue of questions and the rate of each connection; MUST send presence, queue-state and typing frames and a periodic heartbeat; MUST answer a ping; and MUST NOT let a deleted room be recreated by a connection or a turn that races its deletion.

title: Rooms interface
statement: The Rooms page MUST list rooms with their activity, who is online and an unread marker, with search; open a room from a link; rename in place; delete behind a confirmation that states what is lost; export a transcript as Markdown or JSON; show connection and assistant state; reconnect by itself with backoff and rebuild the transcript from the join snapshot; keep a draft per room; show date separators and window long histories; and work on a phone-width screen and with a keyboard.

title: Rooms verification
statement: A live test MUST exercise the room API and WebSocket protocol with several simulated members, including a duplicate display name, a mid-answer join, a rename, a deletion while members are connected and a deletion while the assistant is answering, and MUST leave no room behind.

title: Exact-verifier exit on whole-answer tasks
statement: On tasks whose exact verifier needs the whole answer (code tests, JSON Schema) the adaptive reasoning exit SHOULD probe with a full answer at a lower rate than short probes; a probe that passes the verifier MUST end the reasoning and MAY be returned as the final answer without a further answer stage, and the exit reason MUST be recorded.

title: Retry budget decay and time guard
statement: The thinking budget of verified retry round r SHOULD be budget * decay^r with a configured floor; no System 2 attempt MUST start when the previous attempt's duration exceeds the time left before the request wall-clock cap, and the best candidate so far MUST be returned with a notice instead of a timeout error.
